title: Coastline of One Island
statement:
A map is a grid of 1 (land) and 0 (water) cells, each a 1 × 1 square. The land cells form exactly one island: they are all connected through their up, down, left and right neighbours. Everything outside the grid is water.

Return the length of the island's coastline: the number of unit cell edges that separate a land cell from water or from the outside of the grid. If the island encloses a pond of water, the pond's shore counts too.

examples.why: A plus shape. Each of the four arms has 3 coastal edges; the centre cell is fully surrounded by land.
Not 4 × 4 = 16: the four edges shared between land cells are inland, and each one hides two cell sides.
12 edges on the outside plus 4 around the pond in the middle.

hints: Look at one land cell. Which of its four sides belong to the coastline?
A side is coastline exactly when the neighbour on that side is water or off the grid. No search is needed: every land cell can be checked on its own.
Alternatively: start from 4 × (land cells) and subtract 2 for every pair of land cells that touch.

explain.intuition:
The coastline is made of cell sides, and each side can be judged locally: a side of a land cell is coast if the cell on the other side is water or outside the grid. So walk over every cell, and for each land cell add 1 per side that faces non-land. Connectivity does not matter for the count, so there is no need for DFS.

A tidy variant: every land cell contributes 4 sides, and every place two land cells touch removes 2 of them (one side from each). Check only the right and down neighbours so each touching pair is counted once.
steps: If the cell to its right is land, subtract 2. If the cell below it is land, subtract 2.
pitfalls: Subtracting only 1 per touching pair. The shared edge hides one side of each of the two cells.
Checking all four neighbours and subtracting 2 each time. Then every pair is counted twice.
Forgetting the grid border. A land cell on the edge of the map has coast on that side.

solutions.title: Flood fill and count water sides
solutions.idea: Walk the island with an explicit stack from any land cell. For each land cell visited, count the sides that face water or the outside.

solutions.title: Four per cell, minus shared edges
solutions.idea: Each land cell gives 4 sides; each touching pair of land cells hides 2. Look only right and down so each pair is seen once.

followups: Pond shores should not count, only the outer coast. How would you find which water cells are ponds?
The grid is too big for memory and arrives one row at a time. What do you need to keep between rows?
